rv.q: Forty years after its Broadway debut titillated and outraged American theatergoers, this Harold Pinter masterpiece of family warfare continues to unsettle.
Michael Attenborough's excellent revival gives it a new twist by casting the coolly stylish black actor, Jenny Jules, as the disruptive Ruth.
It's a bleakly horrible psychodrama, delivered with consummate skill.
this ‘Homecoming’ is played like a dark drawing room comedy, skating along the surface of the play. Perhaps there are no depths to be discovered. I begin to wonder.
As a result the shocking ending falls flat and the play’s reputation outshines Mr. Sullivan’s tame production.
